thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 SEV-2: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (region: us-east-1). 5xx spike at 14:03 UTC, 11% failure rate over 1m; p50 latency increased. Paging oncall.
alex (oncall): Acknowledged. I'm on it. @samir @priya pls standby — looks like gateway is returning 502/504s and some long tails on batcher queue.
samir (eng-runtime): I'm pulling scheduler metrics. Seeing batcher queue depth climb on pool gpu-a. KV cache hit rate normal. Any deploys? priya?
priya (sre): No deploys in window. Alerts show sudden request surge + batching backlog. Could be head-of-line (HOL) from a few large seq requests.
jordan (support): Receiving multiple customer tickets for timeouts (timeout at ~30s). Customers: AcmeAnalytics, NoteFlow. They've reported 502s and partial streaming failures.
alex (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) identify top offending client IPs/keys 2) apply temporary rate-limit or route to lower-throughput path 3) lower max_batch_size or enable batch preemption 4) scale up replica pool if needed. I'll start point 1.
samir (eng-runtime): Querying logs for top keys. Running:
```bash
kubectl logs -n inference batcher-gpu-a --since=5m | jq -r '.request | {key, tokens, seq_len}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 20
```
samir (eng-runtime): Found 3 API keys responsible for ~48% of queued tokens, seq_len avg = 1024, tokens per request high. Keys: key-ax9, key-kb3, key-ac2 (redacted). These map to a single customer + a test harness.
alex (oncall): @casey can we temporarily bump dedicated pool capacity in us-east-1? If not, we'll reroute those keys to smaller model or throttle.
casey (eng-platform): Scaling request accepted. I'm kicking an autoscale action (+3 replicas) but that will take ~90s to warm. Also enabling an emergency route to fallback cluster (lower-capacity but fewer HOL problems).
priya (sre): While scaling, let's apply per-key soft rate-limits to key-ax9 and key-kb3 to 30rps. Applying now:
```bash
# apply ephemeral quota
redwoodctl routes quota set --key key-ax9 --rps 30 --duration 10m
redwoodctl routes quota set --key key-kb3 --rps 30 --duration 10m
```
priya (sre): Quotas applied. Monitoring queue depth.
alex (oncall): Observability: p95 latency falling slightly, 5xx rate decreased to ~6% but still above baseline. Queue depth on gpu-a dropping from 420 -> 180 in last 2 minutes.
samir (eng-runtime): Enabling batch preemption (eviction of very long requests) on pool gpu-a for 5 minutes to prevent HOL blocking:
```yaml
# temp config
batcher:
  enable_preemption: true
  preempt_threshold_ms: 8000
  preempt_action: respawn
```
samir (eng-runtime): Patch applied. Preemption logs show evicted 18 long-running items; those caused downstream 504s but reduced HOL.
jordan (support): Notified AcmeAnalytics and NoteFlow with interim update: "We have applied temporary throttles and are scaling the cluster; you may see reduced throughput for your jobs for ~10-20 minutes as we mitigate HOL issues." They acknowledged.
alex (oncall): After preemption + quotas + scale, 5xx now at 2.1%, p95 latency within SLO for most routes. Still seeing occasional gateway 502 from worker restarts during scale.
casey (eng-platform): Autoscale finished. New replicas healthy. I've also rotated the fallback route off and drained the fallback cluster.
samir (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: a small number of heavy sequential requests (large sequence lengths) were batching into long-running batches and blocking the continuous batcher queue. The runtime's current preemption threshold was too permissive for this workload spike. Need follow-ups: - tune preemption to more aggressive on busy pools - add per-key token quotas in routing - improve detection & automatic fallback for oversized sequences.
priya (sre): Post-incident checklist: collect flame graphs for evicted runs, capture batch size distribution before/after, create alert for queue depth > 300 sustained 2m.
mike (customer-ops): Thanks for the quick mitigation. Can you keep me posted on permanent limits? We need to communicate to our customers about best practices for large sequential jobs.
alex (oncall): Will hand off to Samir for postmortem and Casey for infra follow-ups. I'm marking this incident as mitigated and moving to monitoring. Closing notes: timeline, keys involved, commands executed, support notes attached. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident updated: status MITIGATED at 14:23 UTC. Runbook link: https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/batcher-hol
samir (eng-runtime): I'll own the postmortem. I'll include recommendations: default preempt_threshold_ms -> 4000 for high-util pools, add per-key soft quota circuit in router, ensure autoscale warmup policy faster for burst spikes. Will ping when draft is ready.
alex (oncall): Thanks all. If we see a reoccurrence, reactivate pager. Good job. :thumbsup:
